title: EMA-KPO: Simplifying Kalman Policy Optimization with Fixed-Gain Exponential Smoothing

contributions.purpose: Reveals that KPO's supposedly adaptive Kalman filter actually follows a fixed schedule.
contributions.mechanism: Analysis of KPO's Kalman gain dynamics showing that with fixed noise parameters (Q = 1e-6, V = 1) the Kalman gain K_t is deterministic, depending only on token position, not on observations.
contributions.evaluation: The scheduled EMA with alpha_t = K_t is mathematically equivalent to the Kalman filter (MSE < 1e-14).
contributions.domain: RL for LLM reasoning (RLVR) / policy optimization
contributions.source_quote: We analyze KPO's Kalman filter and show that with fixed noise parameters, the Kalman gain follows a deterministic schedule independent of observations.

contributions.purpose: Removes the complexity of covariance state tracking and adaptive gain computation from KPO.
contributions.mechanism: EMA-KPO replaces KPO's Kalman filtering of token-level importance sampling ratios with a scheduled exponential moving average using alpha_t = K_t.
contributions.evaluation: Achieves mathematical equivalence to the Kalman filter (MSE < 1e-14) while eliminating covariance tracking machinery.
contributions.domain: RL for LLM reasoning (RLVR) / policy optimization
contributions.source_quote: We propose EMA-KPO, a simpler alternative that replaces Kalman filtering with a scheduled EMA, achieving mathematical equivalence while eliminating state tracking.

contributions.purpose: Validates that the simplification preserves KPO's performance and stability.
contributions.mechanism: Empirical comparison of EMA-KPO against KPO-clipped on mathematical reasoning benchmarks.
contributions.evaluation: Identical 12.29% on AIME'24 and +1.45pp on MATH-500 versus KPO, while preserving training stability and avoiding the entropy collapse affecting GRPO.
contributions.source_quote: We validate EMA-KPO on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, demonstrating equivalent performance to KPO (identical on AIME'24, +1.45pp on MATH-500) while preserving training stability.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Kalman Policy Optimization (KPO) (He et al., 2026) takes a different approach by applying Kalman filtering to smooth token-level IS ratios ... Our work builds on KPO by analyzing its filtering mechanism and proposing a simpler equivalent formulation.
Based on this observation, we propose EMA-KPO, which replaces the Kalman filter with a scheduled exponential moving average (EMA) using alpha_t = K_t.
Our analysis reveals that KPO's benefits come from low-pass filtering strength, not Kalman-specific adaptive machinery.

notes: Simplification/equivalence paper: main result is a tie with KPO by design (identical AIME'24, +1.45pp MATH-500); contribution is demystifying KPO rather than improving accuracy. Paper carries an automated-research-system generation warning.
